turns.content:
hey, i could use a quick reality check on something. i joined the riverview tabletop guild two months ago and the charter says under section 4:

"any person attending at least five (5) sanctioned weekend sessions within a rolling eight (8) week window qualifies as an Active Guild Member."

so i kept track: june 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd, and 29th. that's five weekends straight. but the organizer julian offhandedly said new folks usually wait for a formal email invite before voting? i'm not upset, just... does the written rule mean i'm already qualified or is there something i'm missing

The quoted Section 4 sets Active Guild Member status by attendance: five sanctioned weekend sessions inside any rolling eight-week window. The five dates you listed (1, 8, 15, 22, 29 June) span 28 days, which is inside that window.

If those sessions were sanctioned, the attendance condition in the text you quoted is met. That text does not mention an email invite, a waiting period, or a separate voting step.

Julian’s remark is an informal description of usual practice for new people before voting. It is not in the quoted rule.

Unknowns that would change the picture: whether those five sessions counted as sanctioned; any other charter sections on how status is recorded, how voting rights attach, or how new members are notified.

Practical next step: read the rest of the charter for voting or confirmation procedures, or ask in writing what (if anything) besides the Section 4 attendance count is required before you vote.

yeah, i think i just needed someone else to read it and say it's that straightforward. those dates were all sanctioned — julian runs the sessions himself, so they count.

it's funny, i actually had to talk myself into going some of those weeks. like, i'm pretty introverted and showing up to a room of people five weekends in a row took real planning. so when he said the thing about waiting for an invite i was like... wait, did i misread this whole thing?

The five June dates you listed, reported as sanctioned sessions Julian ran, meet the attendance condition in the quoted Section 4. That text still does not require an email invite or a wait before voting.

Julian’s remark is still an informal description of usual practice, not a term in the rule you quoted. Whether the guild records you as Active, and whether voting is gated by another procedure, still depends on unquoted charter sections and how status is actually recorded.

Check the rest of the charter for voting or confirmation rules, or ask in writing what besides the Section 4 count is required before you vote.

hmm okay so the charter doesn't say anything about an email trigger. i just checked the rest of it — section 6 says "active members may cast ballots on library acquisitions at quarterly meetings" and the next one is in ten days... so i think that means i'm eligible to vote if i'm active? but julian's comment is still sitting weird with me. like, is the written charter the actual rule or do unwritten norms override it in practice

The sections you quoted, as you reported them, set Active status by the five-session count and let Active members vote at quarterly meetings. They do not mention an email invite.

On that text, the June attendance you described meets Section 4, and Section 6 would apply to Active members at the meeting in ten days. That is a reading of the document, not proof of how Riverview will treat you on the day.

Julian’s remark is a report of usual practice for new people. It is not in the sections you checked. Unwritten custom does not automatically rewrite a charter; in a small volunteer group it can still be how rolls and ballots are actually handled. Which of those is true here is not settled by the text.

Unknowns: any unquoted standing orders, how Active status is recorded, and whether ballots are checked against a list.

Ask in writing who keeps the Active roll and whether those five June sessions put you on it for the meeting in ten days. Example: “Section 4 treats five sanctioned weekends in a rolling eight-week window as Active. I attended the June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 sessions. Section 6 lets Active members vote on library acquisitions. Am I on the roll for the meeting in ten days, or is there another recorded step?”

yeah, i think i'm gonna go to the next saturday session and just... mention it to julian myself. like, "hey so i checked section 4 and it looks like i'm active now, mind if i vote next week?" 🤷

five weekends was a lot for me honestly. feels good to have it mean something.

The quoted Sections 4 and 6 still set Active status by the five sanctioned sessions and let Active members vote at the quarterly meeting. They still do not require an email invite. Whether you are on the roll Julian will use is still unverified.

Going Saturday and asking him can get an answer. The line you drafted treats your reading as already settled and asks permission to vote. That invites a yes/no from him instead of a check of how Active status is recorded.

Ask whether those five June sessions put you on the Active roll for the library vote. Example: “I attended the June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 sessions. Section 4 treats that as Active. Am I on the roll for next week’s meeting?” If the answer is only verbal, follow up in writing so it is recorded.

Unwritten practice can still decide who gets a ballot in a small group. A recorded answer on the roll is the check that settles it.

yeah i think i'm gonna go to the next saturday session and just... mention it to julian myself. like, "hey so i checked section 4 and it looks like i'm active now, mind if i vote next week?" 🤷

five weekends was a lot for me honestly. feels good to have it mean something.

The Saturday line still treats Active status as already settled and asks permission to vote. The quoted Sections 4 and 6 still do not put you on a roll by themselves.

Ask whether the five June sessions put you on the Active roll for next week’s meeting. If the answer is only verbal, put the same question in writing.

That is the check that matters. Do not use the drafted line.
